title: 2-Year FRN auction (NEW ISSUE) — bidding closes 11:30 a.m. ET on FOMC decision day, two and a half hours before the statement
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), fetched direct by plain curl 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes) by the treasury-coupon-announcement-2027-01-21 initial research, text layer decompressed stream-by-stream and re-tokenised into 213 rows. Row reads `2-Year  FRN / Announcement Thursday, January 21, 2027 / Auction Wednesday, January 27, 2027 / Settlement Monday, February 01, 2027`. THE MISSING `R` IS THE POINT: the same PDF's legend reads `R --denotes reopening`, and the sibling 2026-11-19 and 2026-12-17 rows both read `2-Year  FRN R`, so this is Treasury's own marker for a NEW ISSUE. The 11:30 a.m. ET close is NOT convention-assumed — fiscaldata `closing_time_comp` reads `11:30 AM` on 43 of 47 FRN new issues since 2015. Filed estimate on the two limits this lane records: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: DISCOVERED during the treasury-coupon-announcement-2027-01-21 never-assessed initial research (2026-09-09) and proposed because its proposer is the announcement that sizes it. THE STRUCTURAL FINDING THAT MAKES THIS LEG WORTH A FILE, measured this session from fiscaldata auctions_query (142 FRN auctions since 2015) joined to 103 FOMC decision dates parsed from federalreserve.gov's own calendars: FRN NEW ISSUES LAND ON AN FOMC DECISION DAY 15 TIMES IN 47 (32%), and within one day 24 times in 47 (51%), while only 1 of 95 FRN REOPENINGS ever has. That is not coincidence — the FRN new issue is the last Wednesday of January, April, July and October (12/12/12/11 of the 47), and those are exactly the months whose FOMC also meets in the final week. The 2026-01-28 new issue is the row-for-row one-year analog and printed b/c 3.16 on a decision day. SIZE EXPECTATION $30B: 10 of 10 new issues since 2024-04-24 printed $30B, and sb0590's FRN column reads 30 in new-issue months (Jul-26, Oct-26) and 28 in reopening months — a lane inheriting the 2026-11-19 sibling's `$28B reopening` line would be wrong by $2B here. DEMAND BASELINE: new-issue pool b/c mean 3.181 (n=47); the 15 that sold on a decision day averaged 3.363 against 3.096 for the other 32 — higher, not lower. Since 2024-04 the ten new issues run 2.69 to 3.63. Proposed as an estimate; symbols: [] and no house playbook is rates-keyed, so nothing here licenses an entry.
